what: The signature block of an event or task description (shared/signatures.ts): where a block starts (the LAST line that is exactly "-- ", trailing whitespace ignored), what it says, the description without it, and the description with a body applied — replacing, never stacking. Measured from the TypeScript before the port.
why: Both editors insert and remove signatures, on both surfaces, and the blocks must be byte-identical so neither device doubles what the other inserted. A frontend that is not JavaScript has to write the same block. The rule is text only (RFC 5545 DESCRIPTION is TEXT); the core answers strings.
writtenBy: src/state/signatures.measure.test.ts — a one-off, run once and deleted; its cases mirror src/state/signatures.test.ts plus the rows the port needs that those never had: extra trailing whitespace on the marker, an indented marker, three dashes, the marker as first or last line, only the marker, several blank lines before the block, no blank line before it, CRLF text, and the whitespace characters where JavaScript and Rust disagree (NEL U+0085, BOM U+FEFF, NBSP) — DESIGN §4.5 (c): a twin must not lean on a built-in.

whereItLives.note: Inside cal-core, like the other fixtures; a crate reads its own files.

notInThisTable.the auto-signature of a bound calendar: which signature a calendar binds, and the "mine versus theirs" bookkeeping the editors do when the calendar changes (autoSignature ref) — the surface’s; they call these three
notInThisTable.Signature {id, name, body}: a stored record; the name is never sent

shape.texts: {description} → read: the block’s text or null; strip: the description without the block and the blank lines that separated it.
shape.apply: {description, body} → the description with `body` as its block; an empty (whitespace-only) body removes the block; a whitespace-only description is nothing.
shape.lineEndings: Lines are split on LF alone; a CR stays part of its line and counts as trailing whitespace on the marker line.
shape.whitespace: Trailing whitespace on the marker line and the emptiness tests use JavaScript’s whitespace set (WhiteSpace + LineTerminator: includes U+FEFF and U+00A0, excludes U+0085) — pinned by the nel/bom rows.

texts.note: Plain text has no signature; stripping changes nothing.

texts.name: a-block-after-a-blank-line
texts.note: The shape applySignature writes; the blank line goes with the block.

texts.name: the-last-marker-wins
texts.note: A forwarded invitation carries somebody else’s signature above; ours is the one at the end, the same rule mail clients apply.

texts.note: A provider that returns CRLF: the marker is recognised (the CR is trailing whitespace), and the CRs on the other lines stay as they are — the split is on LF alone. Pinned as measured.

texts.name: a-block-with-blank-lines-inside
texts.note: The body keeps its own structure.

texts.name: trailing-nel-on-the-marker-line
texts.note: U+0085 NEXT LINE after the dashes. JavaScript’s trimEnd does NOT remove it (it is not in its whitespace set), so this is NOT a marker there. Pinned so the port cannot lean on Rust’s is_whitespace, which does remove it (DESIGN §4.5 c).

texts.name: trailing-bom-on-the-marker-line
texts.note: U+FEFF after the dashes. JavaScript’s trimEnd DOES remove it (it counts as whitespace there), so this IS a marker; Rust’s is_whitespace would not. Pinned for the same reason.

texts.name: trailing-nbsp-on-the-marker-line
texts.note: U+00A0 after the dashes: whitespace on both sides.
